findings.title: Existing SQL parser/command tests will fail now that TablesList always errors; no regression test added
findings.body:
`TablesList` now always fails, because `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands` returns "not implemented". `NewSQLCommand` calls `TablesList`, so it now always returns a BadRequest error.

The existing tests are not modified in this PR. These are `pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go`, which asserts the table names extracted by `TablesList`, and `pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go`, which expects `NewSQLCommand("a", "select a from foo, bar")` to succeed. They will now fail and break CI.

The tests should be skipped or rewritten to assert the disabled behaviour. A regression test should also be added that a SQL expression is rejected, through both the reader and the `NewSQLCommand` path, even when the `sqlExpressions` flag is on. That locks in the security fix.

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions looks like a flag check but always returns false
findings.body:
The function reads `FlagSqlExpressions`, stores the *negation* in a variable named `enabled`, and then returns `false` from both branches. The flag lookup is dead code.

The name and structure suggest the feature honours the toggle, but it is unconditionally disabled. The misleading `enabled := !...` inversion makes it easy for a future change, such as switching the final `return false` to `return true`, to silently re-enable the code path.

Because this is a security kill-switch, it should be explicit. Either return `false` with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264, or drop the flag lookup entirely. As written, users with the flag on get "sqlExpressions is not implemented" from code that appears to check whether they enabled it.

findings.title: Main query path is not gated; it still runs SQL-building code on user input and relies only on the stub
findings.body:
The new disable check is only in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`, which serves the query-service path. The regular expression path (`buildCMDNode` → `UnmarshalSQLCommand` → `NewSQLCommand`) has no such gate.

On that path, raw user SQL still goes into `sql.TablesList`. That function still builds `SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')` by string formatting user input. It then logs at Error level ("error serializing sql", parser.go:28) together with the raw user SQL on every request.

The only thing preventing execution is that the `DB` stub returns "not implemented". If anyone restores a real `NewInMemoryDB` implementation, the RCE/LFI vector comes back immediately. Meanwhile, users get a misleading 400 "error reading SQL command", and any user can generate Error-level log noise.

Put the hard disable at the top of `NewSQLCommand` (or `UnmarshalSQLCommand`), so no path reaches the SQL parsing or execution code, and return a clear "SQL expressions are disabled" error.
